intelligence.essence: The Inventory is the whole world, organized so you can build NayaNET right now: Part 1, the design laws; Part 2, the pieces — the real gauge, the board (`.ph-card`), the jewel (`.os-jewel` / `.pj-jewel`), the numbers, the pills, the chart-as-boards language, the 478-piece index (truth: 571 unique IDs, 154 canonical in `pieces.json`, live CSS in `factory.css`), the Factory harvest (34 parts from Hub, Personal, the PI face, the canonical pages, the Smart Factory); Part 3, the locked-in smart blocks — viewpoints that land here ONLY when Shawn says "okay yeah it's good" on them live. The method: code HERE, live with him, viewpoint by viewpoint; build piece after piece from the pieces that exist — NEVER start fresh with new code. Copy VERBATIM — never restyle, never rebuild "in the style of." Change only the text inside. High-end only — no Ford parts.
intelligence.human_view: You never start from a blank page. You open the Inventory, you find the piece — the gauge, the board, the jewel, the pill — and you take it exactly as it is, because it is already proven. The board is the same part on Dashboard, Hub, and Personal: same shape, same depth, same lift, the accent changing per page. That is the family. One view done, lock it in as inventory, next view — until the page is done, then the next page.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine a giant toy box where every toy is already built, shiny, and perfect — and you just pick the ones you need and snap them together to make something new. You never have to build a wheel from scratch when the box already has the best wheel in the world. That is the Factory: the box with all the best parts, ready to snap together.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, a good workshop keeps its tools in order — every tool in its place, every piece labeled, nothing lost. That is what this Inventory is: the whole workshop, laid out, so anyone who walks in can build something beautiful without hunting, without guessing, and without making a poor copy of a tool that already exists, perfect, on the shelf.
intelligence.ai_view: You harvest first, never invent. Every path in the Inventory was verified on disk before it was written; a path that could not be verified is marked TO-LOCATE, never guessed — the 7 canonical libraries are still TO-LOCATE, and you do not guess a path for them. A viewpoint lands in Part 3 only on his word, live. When a part earns its place — volume, light, material, shadow, physical touch — it is filed in the Factory, categorized, and reused forevermore. If it is not real, it is not filed.
